💡 Key Takeaways
  • von Next Generation am 24.10.2026 in den Kategorien Champions League,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.
  • Como beat Manchester United 4-1 — and in this case the scoreline really is a fair expression of the game.
  • Cesc Fàbregas’s side demonstrated two things that rarely go together.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

von Next Generation am 24.10.2026 in den Kategorien Champions League,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.

Como beat Manchester United 4-1 — and in this case the scoreline really is a fair expression of the game. For long stretches the match was one-sided, not in terms of chance volume but in terms of access: Como dictated in every phase where the ball went, who received it, and under what conditions it had to be played on. United never got on terms in any of those phases.

Cesc Fàbregas’s side demonstrated two things that rarely go together. Out of possession, a pressing structure with clear direction, isolation of one side, and man-marking that applied near the ball only for the action in progress while everything around it was already speculating on the second ball. And in possession, a positional game of remarkable technical maturity that ties opponents in, switches play, and works systematically into the space behind them. The 4-1 is therefore less an outlier than evidence of work that has been built up over recent seasons.

This analysis goes through the phases one by one: first Como in possession and United’s response, then the work against the ball from the high press to defending the box, and finally the goals.

In build-up, Como moved away from their nominal 4-2-3-1 and sat closer to a 4-3-3, with the eights as the real variable: very free in their movement and above all active in the half-spaces. The base structure stayed stable — a flat four plus a six in front of them, sometimes ahead of the line, sometimes slightly behind the forward line.

Close to their own goal, Como consistently involved goalkeeper Butez as an additional central player in the build-up. That created a five-against-four against United’s front line — awkward on paper, more awkward still in execution, because Como didn’t use the overload to play through but to tie opponents in. From there, the same shape kept appearing on both the right and the left: centre-back, full-back, a player from the half-position in the eight space, and a six alongside. A diamond that wasn’t an end in itself but had a purpose: the diagonal route out.

Como’s build-up structure. From a 4-1 (flat four), the half-positions with Paz and Perrone are added. Small triangles and diamonds emerge. The three attackers ahead of them create additional options in behind.

One detail deserves particular attention. At times the full-backs stood not wide but flat, in a half-position. That sounds like a nuance, but it had a clear function: it vacated the wing and created the space the eights could drop into — Paz and Perrone did so regularly. If you don’t occupy the wing yourself, you force the opponent to guard it anyway.

ManU got no access near the ball and left large diagonal spaces open on the far side.

According to recent reports, for United’s midfielders this was close to unsolvable. Tielemans, Mount and Andrey Santos spent the whole game struggling to establish any responsibility at all, let alone get into duels. When an eight dropped out, they couldn’t follow, and if one of them was tied in by it, a two-against-one opened up on the far wing. Como didn’t create that situation once; they created it serially.

Recent findings suggest that the decisive mechanism lay in receiving and relaying the ball. The player in the deeper position usually worked with two touches: the first took the ball backwards, the second relayed it to the free teammate. At the end of every one of those actions stood a player with the game in front of him — and from that open position he could switch play.

Industry observers note that what made it possible were the preparatory movements. Paz and captain Da Cunha first lured their markers in the wrong direction and then worked with the head start they’d bought. That head start isn’t only space, it’s above all time: time to control the ball first and relay it second, rather than having to do both in one touch.

Recent findings suggest that A scene in the 17th minute is typical. Mason Mount steps out, Mazraoui goes into the duel at the same time — nominally United are in an overload here. Only neither of them really gets to the opponent, because both are too late. Paz can therefore calmly take his touch backwards and switch play directly with the second, dissolving the pressure before it had even formed.

Industry observers note that when the build-up ran down the right, it demonstrated in a recurring pattern: Paz and Da Cunha took the first touch backwards or inside and then switched with the left foot out of a closed body position. The players they found were systematically in open positions — Milla, the far-side six, or the wing-to-wing connection directly.

According to recent reports, in the second half, Como adjusted the shape and more often played with two sixes, to form the diamonds faster and switch to the far-side six faster. Couto stood out in this: the right-back repeatedly played the chip into the six or ten space — six or seven times in a row during one spell. It was mainly Paz who received the ball there and could launch the attack.

In the second half Como focus on those diagonal spaces and look for them mainly with chipped balls.

It has been revealed that especially striking inside the diamond are the rotations between the players. Because of the connections between them, they moved in rotation depending on running path, space and ball movement. The same recurring spaces were re-occupied. Under pressure on the ball carrier, the outer players pushed flat or ran in behind the opponents; the highest player in the diamond burst out of the cover shadow and became the reference point in depth. On a deep pass, the two wide players released and joined the depth, able to offer themselves again immediately in an open body position. If the pass went via the flat wide players, the spaces in front of the new ball carrier could be run into. Every rotation, every positional adjustment was coordinated with the others and, in the end, produced a stream of pressure-resolving passes while Manchester United chased the press in vain.

Como bridged the middle third exceptionally promptly, via dribbles at speed and diagonal passes. Behind it stood a recognisable principle: first tie the opponent to one wing, then get behind them via the diagonal, and in the final third do the same thing again. In sum, that produced the shape of a Z — build-up on the right, transition on the left, finish from the right again.

In this example Como pin ManU in the press with their short passing. Thanks to the extra attacker on the ball-near side they can play through the pressure and switch.

Sources indicate that the connections between wingers and striker carried these attacks and were deliberately kept flexible. The wide players sometimes stayed wide, sometimes came short, sometimes tucked inside. Douvikas accordingly either waited deep in front of the line for the chipped ball or, when space opened up on the wing, received the deeper pass and then ran in behind along the wing as soon as the ball sat on the full-back’s open foot. That flexibility produced the overloads on one side, and the overloads produced the central overload.

It has been revealed that in the final third one element was added that is rare in fast transition teams: patience. Como drew opponents towards them with dribbles and short passes, used back-passes when needed, and then switched in front of the block. Da Cunha, Baturina and Paz were the three who could tie opponents in and then find the diagonal. They created the positions on the diagonal, were available to receive, and used their space to apply pressure. The block was usually tied in with short touches, the switch and the position behind the opponent prepared, and quick finishes sought.

The intensity in possession shouldn’t be underestimated. Practically every attack involved at least three or four players, the width was occupied, the centre likewise, and there were multiple options throughout. What they looked for almost every time was the space behind the opponent on the far side — exactly the zone that is closed last when a block shifts across.

According to recent reports, paz brought the right profile for this pattern. A strong left foot cutting inside from the right, he repeatedly dropped into the right-hand blind side of his opponents, got shots away there with few touches, and racked up the most shots of the match. That the finishes generally came off few touches isn’t a detail but the consequence of the time won further back.

It has been revealed that as the move continues, Como again look for the blind side of the defenders. Here Douvikas and Paz are positioned in behind, with Da Cunha joining in front of the back line. After briefly pinning the opponents, the switch reaches Da Cunha, who misses the target from distance.

According to recent reports, what carries all of this is the technical execution. Soft passes, sharp ones when the moment called for it, consistently well timed and played into the right foot — for ninety minutes. Passing that secure at that tempo is what makes a variable concept actually retrievable.

Sources indicate that united’s basic problem out of possession was the hybrid. They pressed half man-oriented, but with a plus-one in the last line — a construction that forces compromises in both directions. It demands access up front that it doesn’t fund at the back.

There were certainly moments when it worked. When Dalot pushed through into the press on the right and passed his man backwards, a clean man-orientation emerged all the way up to the front — and with it a clear assignment for Mount, out of which the ball could be won. But that stayed the exception. Most of the time Dalot sat too flat out of possession, so United couldn’t trigger the duels up front and went into the press a man short.

Sources indicate that mount was the most conspicuous case in this respect. He barely got into a duel across the whole match because the decision to step out always came too late. Against a team that works with preparatory movements, a late decision is practically the same as none: the opponent already has the head start before the journey even begins.

On top of that came a problem on the far side. There, United’s winger frequently failed to protect the depth — usually Mbeumo, who jogged back rather than closing the space. But that was precisely the target zone of Como’s diagonal switches. It allowed them to change sides almost at will and regularly find an open structure on the other side.

In a recent development, the second half brought no improvement. The distances to opponents stayed large, and centrally what was actually intended still didn’t materialise. Michael Carrick’s double change at half-time was meant to bring more physicality to the six with Carlos Baleba, but it didn’t solve the problem — the assignments still didn’t work, the duels in the centre still didn’t happen, and the wide positions dragged the eights out further, which opened new spaces.

In the end the energy simply wasn’t there to press with the necessary intensity. United’s press became increasingly static, and a static press against an opponent with this passing quality yields not a single ball win — it only hands them the starting positions they’re looking for anyway.

It has been revealed that como started the game in a high press and sustained it above all in the first half, with isolated spells after the break too. It was triggered on back-passes and goal kicks — and, remarkably, by their own goals: after every strike the team immediately pushed high again instead of managing the lead in a deeper block.

In a recent development, the steering ran consistently towards United’s left build-up side. The reason is personnel: Harry Maguire played there with his weaker left foot as the outside foot, and next to him stood another right-footer in Noussair Mazraoui on the left. Two right-footers on one build-up side means the ball always has to be taken back inside to play on — exactly where Como were closing the door. The press was usually triggered by the left-sided forward, with the ball ending up at either Maguire or Mazraoui.

Pressing structure after the change in the second half.

In the centre Como defended man-oriented, with both sixes pushing very high and taking flat passes into United’s midfielders out of the game. That removed the short route through the middle as an option and left the long ball. But the long ball triggered nothing for United: the second balls went to Como practically every time.

That isn’t chance, it’s running work. The sixes consistently tracked the negative pressing paths back, anticipated the long ball early, and were in front of the line before it arrived. Luis Milla covered the most ground of any player on the pitch in this pattern — recovery runs after being played past, doubling up on the ball, attacking the second ball. When the long ball came from Maguire or one of the full-backs, a six was regularly in front of the line with an intense sprint, sealing the centre, taking away the diagonal follow-up passes and attacking the loose balls.

Defending the long ball and extra support on the second ball.

Once the ball was on one side, that side was isolated. The near-side forward had access to the centre-back and dropped back a touch when the pass went to the full-back, so that he covered centre-back and six simultaneously and closed the square pass. The far-side forward marked the goalkeeper. That served two functions at once: it took away United’s escape route via the keeper along with the switch, and it kept a player in position for the moment of the turnover.

Recent findings suggest that the double pivot worked in a deliberate half-position. The near-side six stayed tight to his man, the far-side one dropped slightly behind him — securing the space and at the same time establishing access to the far-side centre-back in United’s back three.

In a recent development, the last line defended largely man-for-man in the high press, and very tightly. But the decisive detail is the one that carries the whole concept: the man-marking near the ball applied only to the action in progress. Around it, players were already releasing from their assignments and orienting towards the second ball. That is only retrievable at very high intensity — and it’s the reason United’s forced long balls produced not a single usable moment.

Recent findings suggest that when Como dropped a line, the man-orientation at the second height stayed exceptionally high. Here too the back-pass served as the trigger to push up as a unit and tip back into man-marking. If United were in a closed body position, the Comaschi had already pushed up far enough to attack the back-pass at the moment it was played — a pattern that led directly to the 3-0. The half-position was at work there again: closing down level with the centre-back while simultaneously prepared to push through onto the next player deeper.

Recent findings suggest that in the first half Como still had problems assigning the half-positions against ManU’s 3-2-5. In this example Fernandes moves to the wing, Como fail to establish responsibility and access and are played through at mid-height.

Sources indicate that up to half-time, though, Como had a structural problem with this. The pure man-marking didn’t come off cleanly, because of the two sixes in front of the line, one should really have tucked in and taken over the half-position for the centre-backs. That didn’t happen consistently. The consequence: a centre-back stepped out, the space behind him stayed unoccupied, and that was exactly what United kept attacking.

According to recent reports, the pattern of pressing onto Manchester United’s left side continued in the second half, now with Dalot at full-back. The press was still triggered by Douvikas, with the ball-near winger pushing up as a second striker to press the centre-back. Paz focused on the visitors’ ball-near six and Couto pushed through onto Dalot. Through the central connections the game was isolated on one side.

It has been revealed that at half-time Como adjusted. One six moved directly into the line, with the far-side winger pushing in onto the six — they now pressed out of a 5-2-1-2. Lucas Da Cunha pressed through from the right onto Maguire, while Nico Paz picked up United’s six. The central forward pressed the central centre-back and from there carried on to the goalkeeper. The far-side wide midfielder and the remaining six were poised — one onto United’s free six, one onto the far-side centre-back — again in that half-position between opponent and the space to be protected.

ManU building up high against the man-oriented Italians.

The effect was immediately visible. Como controlled the half-positions, got access right into the last line throughout, and set the rhythm of the match from then on. The adjustment solved exactly the problem the first half had left open, without changing the underlying principle.

In the final phase Como defended from a very deep line inside the box. That left barely any space behind the line to play into — which United hardly looked for anyway. The visitors attacked little depth and rarely occupied the width in the final third, so Como could stay compact without being punished for it.

Accordingly, a lot of players stood very centrally in and in front of the box. That produced numerous cover shadows and a numerical superiority around the ball, which allowed them to steer actively within the block rather than merely react. At times they deliberately steered inside, to guide the opponent into the prepared congestion and cover from a deeper position.

Deep back line in the box, centre closed and play steered inside. The box defending allowed the English side shots from distance.

In a recent development, the crucial point is that Como left the gaps open not despite this set-up but because of it. If you pack the box and secure the depth, you give up the space in front of the line — and that is exactly where United were supposed to shoot from.

In a recent development, the numbers vindicate the decision. Taking the conceded goal out of the box, Como allowed nine shots from outside the penalty area across ninety minutes, worth roughly 0.24 xG combined; only three of them were even on target. On top of that, of the four shots inside the box, two came from at least 14 to 15 metres and effectively belong in the long-range category as well. United accepted the invitation, and the shooting quality was perfectly decent — it’s just that with that scoring probability over a whole match, the most likely outcome is precisely what happened.

Tracking the ball for the first goal.

1-0, Nico Paz (2′) — The goal comes before United are even set. Como take the goal kick rapidly and play straight to the full-back, luring the visitors into the press — only not cleanly. Mason Mount triggers the pressure and is played past, and on the second ball he goes into the duel as well instead of holding the middle and looking for the space where he could pick the ball up. That is exactly what opens the centre, the space for the second ball is there, and Paz can play it through.

According to recent reports, what follows is the transition principle in its purest form: a quick switch to the diagonal side, then short passes against a very deep line. Matheus Cunha doesn’t pick up the player behind him and leaves the ten space open, where Paz is standing. He needs two touches because neither Cunha from above nor Maguire from his distance gets into the duel. Lammens, for his part, doesn’t defend the goal with his cover shadow but takes the near post — which leaves the far corner to a strong left foot. The curled finish into it is quality, though.

Recent findings suggest that 2-0, Anastasios Douvikas (49′, assist Paz) — Same zone, same cause. Bryan Mbeumo doesn’t choose to shut the centre but closes the centre-back, which creates the space for Da Cunha, who drives forward and plays Martin Baturina in. Centrally, Mount again fails to pick up his man. Out wide, Amad Diallo, introduced at half-time, generates no pressure centrally, so Mazraoui can’t take over the deep wide player in the first place.

It has been revealed that the result is Paz behind the opponent, in the ten space, dribbling unopposed at goal. Matthijs de Ligt establishes no reference to Douvikas’s run in behind and slips as well — a one-against-one with the goalkeeper that Douvikas finishes coolly.

Industry observers note that 3-0, Nico Paz (57′) — The only goal that comes directly out of the work against the ball. Como are in the midfield press in a closed position with access to the inside lane, win the ball there and punish a lapse of concentration in the visitors’ build-up. At the end, Paz is alone in front of Lammens again.

Sources indicate that 4-0, Jacobo Ramón (76′, assist Kaiki) — This goal comes from a longer possession spell and indicates the assignment problem in its clearest form. Mazraoui is too narrow and has no access to the wide player. Diallo stands in the space with access to neither the central player nor the full-back nor the winger — an orientation that doesn’t work in any direction.

Como switch to Máximo Perrone, who can slide the ball out wide because the space is simply free. From there comes the cross from an open body position, and in the centre Como run a two-against-one at the end of which Ramón scores.

It has been revealed that 4-1, Joshua Zirkzee (90′) — Como’s only lapse, and one in a phase in which the team had already dropped very deep. United get the ball to the wing, it’s two against two in the box, and the cross is initially only feinted. Zirkzee orients himself well forwards at that moment, while Como’s defenders are already stepping out after the feinted cross. Diallo’s ball in behind the line is strong, the offside call is razor-thin in his favour, and Zirkzee takes two touches before finishing one-against-one with the goalkeeper. A blemish, not a structural problem.

Sources indicate that the common denominator — Three of Como’s four goals come in the same zone: the space in front of and behind United’s line that nobody takes responsibility for. Mount is involved in two of those scenes through an assignment he never establishes, Diallo in two more after coming on. Nico Paz is at the heart of three of the four goals, twice as scorer, once as the provider — always out of the opponent’s blind side.

Como’s 4-1 has one common cause across every phase, and it lies less in any single idea than in its execution under continuous load. Out of possession they steered, isolated and speculated on the second ball — with man-marking that applied near the ball only for the action in progress and was already dissolved around it. In possession they tied opponents in, switched play and worked systematically into the space behind. Both require eleven players to anticipate a teammate’s decision, and both functioned over the full distance.

In a recent development, the connecting detail is the half-position. In the press, the far-side six stood between opponent and the space to be protected; in possession, the eights worked out of the same zone, and the full-backs occupied it flat in order to vacate the wing for exactly those players. Como, in other words, occupied the position in both directions from which two jobs can be done at once — which is why the side could neither be played past in the press nor be pinned in the build-up.

Industry observers note that for United the diagnosis is more uncomfortable than the result. The problem wasn’t individual errors but that the team never, in any phase, got into the duels it needed. The mixture of half man-orientation and a plus-one in the last line funded no access up front, and without access every decision is made too late — from Mount in the centre to Mbeumo failing to secure the far-side depth. Carrick’s double change at half-time was meant to bring physicality to the six with Carlos Baleba, but it changed nothing about the assignments, and in Diallo a player came on wide who reached neither one opponent nor the other in his space. That the energy ran out in the end was a consequence rather than a cause.

According to recent reports, that leaves the context. A 4-1 against Manchester United is no proof in itself, and Como’s finishing was exceptionally efficient on the night. What revealed regardless of the result, though, is a team with a recognisable, rehearsed answer in all four phases of the game — and one that put a technical maturity on the pitch in possession that you wouldn’t readily credit to a side promoted two years ago.

Les Verts ont le moins de trous d'air

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (388 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Poteaux-carres

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ancien défenseur des Verts, le consultant de beIN Sports Patrice Ferri (63 ans) s'est confié à L'Union avant le déplacement de l'ASSE à Reims programmé après-demain soir.
  • "Sainté, c'est la seule véritable équipe à avoir le moins de trous d'air possible et qui parvient à tenir la distance.
  • A Saint-Etienne, la pression fait partie du club, du package.

Ancien défenseur des Verts, le consultant de beIN Sports Patrice Ferri (63 ans) s'est confié à L'Union avant le déplacement de l'ASSE à Reims programmé après-demain soir. Extraits.

"Sainté, c'est la seule véritable équipe à avoir le moins de trous d'air possible et qui parvient à tenir la distance. C'est ce qu'il faut prendre en compte. Et il y a quelque chose de supplémentaire à Saint-Etienne, c'est l'engouement du public. Comme si l'équipe jouait le haut du tableau de Ligue 1. C’est un élément qui peut faire la différence, bien sûr. Mais ces clubs-là, qui ont une grosse pression, ça peut aussi les perturber à un moment donné. Ceux qui y ont été formés comme ça a été mon cas, ils connaissent très vite cet univers. Tout va plus vite dans ce club. On est tout de suite plongé dans ce milieu professionnel où les résultats sont attendus, où l'engagement de l'équipe est scruté à chaque instant. C'est comme une pieuvre.

A Saint-Etienne, la pression fait partie du club, du package. C'est comme si tu signais au PSG actuellement. C'est la même situation. Le Stade de Reims et l’ASSE ne sont pas totalement dans les mêmes dispositions en termes d'attente. Je ne suis pas persuadé que c'était tout de suite l'idée impérative du Stade de Reims de remonter. Ce n'est pas une obligation ni une nécessité, que ce soit économique ou sportive. Ils ne sont pas dans la même configuration que Saint-Etienne. Quand tu as 35 000 spectateurs au stade en Ligue 2, on se doute bien que le club ne peut pas rester des années dans la division.

In a recent development, le match de ce samedi, ça fait partie des grosses rencontres. Tout le monde trouverait normal que ce soit un match de Ligue 1. Saint-Etienne a besoin de continuer à creuser l'écart qui est loin d'être énorme. De son côté, Reims a la nécessité de faire bonne figure et de réaliser un gros match. Ne serait-ce que par rapport à l'affiche, mais surtout pour ne pas se faire décrocher du top 5. Pour moi, à part Saint-Etienne, pour les autres, ce serait une erreur de vouloir uniquement se positionner pour le top 2. Les matchs sont tellement compliqués que c'est difficile de faire des séries. C'est devenu trop difficile à maîtriser.".

Suivant de près l'actualité du MHSC, Benjamin Psaume est revenu dans le podcast Montpellier Sport Club (relayé par Allez Paillade) sur le match de Coupe de France qui a vu les Héraultais écraser (5-0) le FC Balagne en Corse. L'ancien joueur de Toulouse, Nîmes, Arles-Avignon, Troyes et Le Puy ne tarit pas d'éloges sur Zoumana Camara :.

According to recent reports, "En coupe de France, dans des matchs comme cela où il manque beaucoup de monde, le plus important c’est la qualification. Zoumana Camara a lancé des jeunes. C’est à l’image de ce qu’il montre depuis le début de saison. Il a tellement fédéré le groupe et le vestiaire que peu importe les joueurs qu’il peut mettre, on sent qu’ils sont animés par une envie. Ils ne réfléchissent pas au contexte même s’il est particulier, ils ont envie de faire mal à l’adversaire. Ils ont un enthousiasme dès la première minute. Ils répondent présents. Et quand tu marques à la première minute dans des matchs comme ça, je me suis dit que c’était terminé même si après ils ont eu des occasions. Quand tu es le gros face au “petit”, tu sais que si tu ouvres le score c’est plus facile.

In a recent development, le football a changé car avant, ils mettaient le bus et là tu arrives à les prendre dans la profondeur au bout d’une minute. Cela n’existait pas à mon époque quand tu allais jouer chez une équipe de niveau inférieur. Il n’y a pas eu trop de coups, le synthétique n’a pas joué de mauvais tour non plus. Il n’y a pas eu l’ambiance corse qu’il y avait avant. Tu te rends le match facile. On a découvert des jeunes joueurs. Ils ont réussi sur un tour où on ne leur en aurait pas voulu sur la manière à la mettre pour l’emporter en respectant l’adversaire. Ils ont donné une bonne image du club, ils ont également laissé la recette. À deux ou trois à zéro, ils ont continué. Ce vestiaire, ce groupe là, dans la psychologie, cela m’aurait étonné qu’ils prennent le match de haut. C’est très intéressant et à l’image de ce que l’on voit depuis le début de la saison.".

#61783. Latest Update: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

📅 22 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 25m • 📚 Deep Dive (4980 w)

Latest Update: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

📅 22 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4980 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur.
  • Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.
  • But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their substantial-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

It has been revealed that sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

“He is a top player, no doubt about it,” remarked head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

“He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”.

Recent findings suggest that A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the latest season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh.

Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a substantial cheer from the home fans.

Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

He lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

Sources indicate that richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

Recent findings suggest that vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ.

De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

Bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU.

Igor Thiago missed a penalty after substitute Rodrigo Bentancur fouled Kevin Schade, as Spurs threatened to completely collapse with the result already pretty much decided.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h.

De Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will promptly look a lot different. There are more newly introduced faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that big-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his upcoming-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on latest players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow latest signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

His team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

“You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

“We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a latest project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

“I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

“Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

It has been revealed that “We can improve swiftly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] new players but we have to put something more.

“We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve promptly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an vital defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”.

We had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

Industry observers note that it was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of fresh players. To become a team I said before the game we need two things, soul and style of play. We didn’t fight in the right way. Brentford is maybe one of the most key teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

Sources indicate that it was a game, especially in the first half, in one direction. We were not in the right position to make the high pressure, with Mikey Moore on the left centre.

Sources indicate that we didn’t play well, we didn’t play in the right way. I think not because we don’t remember last season, because these players are good people but we lost too many duels. One of the best qualities of Brentford is the one-to-one, the man-to-man and the set-pieces.

In a recent development, really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can quickly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

Our fans were amazing today. There is a genuine connection here that helps. I thought we started the game brilliantly and they were fully engaged. We want to be relentless. We looked like a real team.

Recent findings suggest that that’s what we wanted, we wanted to start sharp, we want to show people what we’re made of and we did that today. We know last season we were one point off, this year, we’ve added quality people to the squad.

Sources indicate that he’s been unbelievable, I can’t praise him high enough. He’s one of them players that we might lose the ball you just know he is going to win it back and he gets us on the counter-attack so promptly.

Is that Pedro Porro, Micky Van de Ven and Mohammed Kudus could be back for the next game against Newcastle, and Savinho ought to be through the door.

Recent findings suggest that according to Opta, Brentford won the xG battle 3.96 to 0.47, taking 26 shots to Spurs’s nine. De Zerbi’s team finished the game with 59 per cent possession, but that is inflated by Brentford sitting off when three up. It’s the most xG Spurs have conceded in a single game since a 6-3 defeat by Liverpool in December 2024.

Less Christ the Redeemer more Christ, that was terrible.

"I think that sums it up"Fair to say this Spurs fan wasn't pleased with their performance 😅 pic.twitter.com/ZAdVaVbjlS.

It has been revealed that possibly Brentford’s best performance under Keith Andrews, though that may be overstating the strength of the opposition. This was a complete display: they pressed Spurs, they played through Spurs, they played over Spurs, they dominated Spurs from set-pieces and their defenders bullied Spurs’s forwards. It will be interesting to hear from De Zerbi and whether he is philosophical or irate. This is far from Spurs’s ideal projected team, but still unacceptable.

According to recent reports, kinsky palms away a Damsgaard corner, and Yarmoliuk slices his shot over the bar. We are deep into stoppage time, and Brentford’s players are still pressing Bentnacur and Senesi and making them play with their heads down.

According to recent reports, just four minutes of added time to play but Spurs have more defending to do in the shape over another Brentford corner. They survive, but Brentford promptly establish possession again.

It would appear Lord Sugar is still watching:.

Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the massive spenders.

That is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s upcoming leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

In a recent development, spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

It has been revealed that “He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”.

Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

Les All Blacks c'est l'ambiance de Geoffroy-Guichard

À l’occasion du podcast Montpellier Sport Club, disponible en vidéo et en audio depuis ce jeudi 19 novembre sur le site du journal Midi Libre, l’entraîneur du MHSC Zoumana Camara a raconté comment il avait puisé dans ses souvenirs d’un haka des All Blacks et la réaction du XV de France pour préparer le déplacement de son équipe à Saint-Étienne.

Recent findings suggest that "Je me nourris de tout." Comme de nombreux entraîneurs, Zoumana Camara aime aller puiser dans d’autres sports pour nourrir sa méthode. Amateur de basket-ball NBA, de handball ou d’athlétisme, dont il admire le fait de se "préparer pour une compétition qui dure 1’30, un saut, dix secondes", le coach du MHSC regarde également du côté du rugby international. Une source ovale au sein de laquelle il a récemment déniché une inspiration.

"Quand on a préparé Saint-Étienne et qu’on est allés jouer là-bas (le 5 septembre), je sais que j’ai une jeune équipe, qu’on va jouer à Geoffroy-Guichard où l’ambiance est un douzième homme. Alors j’ai voulu faire une causerie un peu différente. Elle m’est venue le matin (du match). Je me suis souvenu que lorsque j’étais plus jeune, j’avais aimé la France lorsqu’elle avait affronté les All Blacks, face à face au moment du haka (en 2007). Et je voulais montrer à mes joueurs que l’environnement, il faut l’affronter de face avant que le match commence et leur dire que les All Blacks, ce sera l’ambiance de Geoffroy-Guichard", détaille-t-il.

À cette comparaison s’est également ajouté un changement d’habitude. "Pour la première fois, j’ai dit au staff d’aller faire l’échauffement à côté du Kop (des Verts). Et pas en plein milieu, pour ne pas fuir", explique Zoumana Camara.

According to recent reports, le Patriote, édition Beaujolais Val de Saône, aussitôt la victoire des Verts acquise à Rumilly, signifiant un ASSE-FCVB pour le 8ème tour de la Coupe de France, est revenu 16 ans en arrière. Il fait un flash-back sur cette rencontre du 3 février 2010, qui avait vu les Verts l'emporter péniblement sur les Caladois (2-2 ap pro, 1-3 aux tab) en 16ème de finale de cette même Coupe de France.

Sources indicate that "L'histoire qui recommence. Seize ans ont passés, depuis la dernière fête du FCVB en Coupe de France, et la venue de l'AS Saint-Etienne à Armand-Chouffet pour le compte des 16es-de-finale d'une épreuve qui avait attiré plus de 3000 personnes en Calade, comme on se donne rendez-vous pour un événement majeur dans une vie de football.Cela avait été une douleur infinie et mémorable pour le groupe du coach Jean-Michel Picollet – lui-même cœur stéphanois – mais les coéquipiers du portier si constant, Franck Laurent, s'étaient construits des souvenirs pour toute une vie. La leur. Et aujourd'hui, ce sont leurs héritiers, plus à la peine en Ligue 3, qui ont gagné le droit de défier l'ASSE, ce gros bras de la Ligue 2, dans moins de quinze jours au stade mythique de Geoffroy-Guichard.".

Pour rappel, l'ASSE alignait la composition suivante : Planté - Dos Reis, Diakhité, Monsoreau, N'Daw - Matuidi, Guilavogui, Mirallas (Payet, 72ème) - Bergessio (Rivière, 94ème)., Sanogo, SakoButs : Bergessio (10ème), Sako (85ème)Tirs au but : Sanogo, Rivière, Payet (seuls 3 tirs au but avaient été nécessaires).

Industry observers note that dans Le Patriote, édition Beaujolais Val de Saône, Philippe Terrier, le Président du FC Villefranche Beaujolais qui va affronter l'ASSE pour le compte du 8ème tour de la Coupe de France le samedi 28 novembre à 20 h, se dit partagé entre joie et soulagement de ne pas avoir à gérer l'organisation d'une telle affiche. Le chef de file du FCVB a résumé le sentiment du jour que beaucoup de Caladois devraient partager dans les jours à venir :.

It has been revealed that "C'est un vrai bonheur pour nous tous ! On s'attend à un match compliqué mais on ne veut pas que l'histoire s'arrête là. On va vivre quelque chose d'extraordinaire, après avoir découvert le Groupama Stadium face au PSG, en 2019, on va connaître Geoffroy-Guichard ! C'est extraordinaire pour le FCVB.".

Une affiche qui convoque quelques souvenirs, en Calade. L'un des plus drôles concerne aussi Philippe Terrier, puisque c'est lors de la venue de Saint-Etienne en 2010 à Villefranche, que l'actuel président du FCVB avait sauté dans le bain de ses actuelles responsabilités pour prendre un poste que l'un de ses illustres prédécesseurs, Jean Gachon avait si bien occupé, des années durant" précise Le Patriote.

Feyenoord preserved their four-point advantage over champions PSV after coming away with a point from Eindhoven thanks to an improved second-half performance.

PSV dominated the first half as they deployed a close-passing, tiki-taka style to stifle Feyenoord, but only had Guus Til’s well-taken volley after 20 minutes to show for it.

Ten minutes after the break Feyenoord equalised when Anis Hadj Moussa was given too much space to charge down the right flank and bend a shot inside the far post.

The Algerian had a good chance for a second towards the end, while PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar had to be alert to keep out a header by Nacho Ferri from close range.

“We were by far the better team today and had the better chances,” said PSV coach Peter Bosz. “We started the second half badly and made a mistake, after which Hadj Moussa scored. And even then we could have won it.”.

According to recent reports, ajax overtook PSV to close the gap at the top to three points with a hard-fought win at Sparta. Veteran striker Jens Toornstra scored for Sparta on his 500th Eredivisie appearance, but Abdellah Ouazane and Tolu Arokodare, the scorers against Atalanta in midweek, were on target again to claim the win for Ajax.

Twente moved up to fourth place as two late goals by Sondre Ørjasæter and Lucas Vennegoor of Hesselink earned a 2-0 win at AZ Alkmaar, who like Twente and PSV have 20 points.

Fortuna Sittard also snatched the points late on against Excelsior as Rodrigo Guth headed in a corner in injury time to keep the Limburg club in sixth place, two points further back.

At the other end of the table, the return of Adrie Koster as veteran coach brought no relief to Willem II, who crashed to a 6-1 home defeat to Cambuur.

The Tilburgers remain four points behind ADO Den Haag, who were unable to keep up the momentum of last week’s win against PSV as they lost 3-2 at home to Heerenveen.

Telstar lost by the same margin at Go Ahead Eagles, whose striker Søren Tengstedt netted twice in the first half to lead the Eredivisie scoring charts with eight goals.

Willem II Tilburg 1-6 Cambuur Leeuwarden.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic new look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

The Manchester City striker revealed his fresh buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP.

Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

Haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a upcoming campaign.

It is a latest-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a fresh Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager mentioned. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many crucial things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

Industry observers note that “When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”.

Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

According to recent reports, “It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”.

Sports club members becoming less tolerant of homosexuality

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Acceptance of homosexuality in Dutch sports clubs has declined significantly in the last generation, according to a survey of attitudes by the Mulier Institute.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Acceptance of homosexuality in Dutch sports clubs has declined significantly in the last generation, according to a survey of attitudes by the Mulier Institute.

The organisation found that 66% of people had no objection to a fellow member of a sports club being gay, while in 2008 the figure was 85%.

Just over half (55%) of respondents remarked they had no problem sharing a shower with a gay team-mate of the same sex, which also represented a drop from 73% in 2008.

The Mulier Institute said the findings reflected a social trend that has also been seen in schools, where the proportion of boys aged between 12 and 16 with a positive view of homosexuality has dropped from 40% to 22% since 2021.

The Dutch Olympic Committee NOC*NSF mentioned the findings were “highly regrettable” and pledged to step up its efforts to make sport more inclusive.

But the John Blankenstein Foundation, which campaigns for LGBT emancipation in sport, said it had noticed declining enthusiasm for its workshops and growing numbers of parents who voiced objections.

Karin Blankenstein, who set up the organisation in 2008, told NOS: “I get the sensitivity around transgender people in sport at the top level, but this is about amateur sport.”.

C'est un match qui donne envie

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (506 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Poteaux-carres

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ecrasé 6-0 lors de sa dernière confrontation avec l'ASSE, l'ancien coach palois et actuel entraîneur rémois Nicolas Usaï s'est exprimé en conférence de presse avant de recevoir les leaders stéphanois après demain-soir lors de la 13e journée de L2.
  • Recent findings suggest that "On prépare un match de haut niveau face à certainement la meilleure équipe au vu de ce qui se passe depuis le début de saison.
  • In a recent development, il n’y a pas de préparation particulière par rapport à cette affiche.

Ecrasé 6-0 lors de sa dernière confrontation avec l'ASSE, l'ancien coach palois et actuel entraîneur rémois Nicolas Usaï s'est exprimé en conférence de presse avant de recevoir les leaders stéphanois après demain-soir lors de la 13e journée de L2.

Recent findings suggest that "On prépare un match de haut niveau face à certainement la meilleure équipe au vu de ce qui se passe depuis le début de saison. Notre groupe a été complété en début de semaine par des jeunes qui nous amènent toujours cet enthousiasme, cette volonté de mettre beaucoup d'intensité dans tout ce qu'ils font. On est très heureux de retrouver nos internationaux dans des conditions plutôt optimales, quand on pense par exemple à Samuel Kotto et Daouda Guindo, qui ont joué et qualifié leur pays pour la CAN. Mohamed Daramy a fait deux matchs avec le Danemark, et ce sont des matchs de très haut niveau. Au lieu de regarder le verre à moitié vide en disant qu’on n'a pas pu travailler avec eux, il faut se servir de leur expérience du très haut niveau avec beaucoup d'enthousiasme et beaucoup d'envie pour préparer ce magnifique match qui se présente samedi.

In a recent development, il n’y a pas de préparation particulière par rapport à cette affiche. Juste, l'important c'est qu'on soit enthousiastes, qu'on soit audacieux dans la préparation d'un match comme ça, et qu'on ait vraiment la volonté de jouer à notre meilleur niveau, mais avec beaucoup de passion et beaucoup de plaisir. Si Saint-Etienne est l'équipe la plus complète aujourd'hui ? Oui, c'est une équipe qui est très complète et qui, dans les moments forts, est très clinique. Elle est très efficace, elle marque beaucoup de buts, elle en encaisse peu. C’est un adversaire de haut niveau. L’idée, c’est de pouvoir se confronter à un rapport de force peut-être plus élevé par rapport à ce qui se dit depuis le début de l'année, être au niveau et avoir envie de s'étalonner. On sait les ingrédients qu'on doit mettre pour faire en sorte de performer.

On sait que ça se joue aussi sur des détails. Sur ces détails-là, il va falloir être très vigilant. L'idée, c'est qu'on soit tous en éveil : le staff, les 20 joueurs qui auront le privilège d'être convoqués pour ce match-là. Mais encore une fois, le mot enthousiasme, ça va être le mot important. On va jouer chez nous, devant nos supporters. Je crois qu'il y a 16 000 ou 17 000 personnes qui sont annoncées. On doit être super heureux de jouer des affiches comme ça. Bien sûr que c’est un rendez-vous excitant à préparer. On parle beaucoup, mais l'idée, c'est d'être présent et d'être performant à l'instant T avec l'envie de poser des problèmes à cette équipe par notre capacité à maîtriser le ballon, à mettre de la vitesse, et que chaque joueur, individuellement et au service du collectif, on soit tous à notre meilleur niveau. C'est un choc entre deux places fortes du football français. C'est un match qui donne envie.".

#61768. Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

📅 23 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 26m • 📚 Deep Dive (5172 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

📅 23 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5172 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning.
  • The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image.
  • All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

Recent findings suggest that joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur.

“It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca stated, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”.

According to recent reports, his team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

In a recent development, marco Rose, their upcoming manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he mentioned. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”.

Recent findings suggest that his team revealed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, fresh signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

According to recent reports, they could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his fresh manager.

Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “newly introduced Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

In a recent development, there was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a latest season? It has been revealed that brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he said of Guardiola’s grand design.

Tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s massive idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

Sources indicate that describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

In a recent development, the Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for upcoming signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

Welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a latest era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut….

The Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

Brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, après le carton de son livre Foot Sentimental paru il y a 3 ans aux éditions Le Cherche midi, Dominique Rocheteau a fait paraître le mois dernier dans la même maison Soif d'Idéal. Dans ce bouquin, l'Ange Vert rend hommage à Bernard Pivot.

"Avant chaque phase finale de Coupe du Monde, Bernard Pivot nous préparait plusieurs valises remplies de livres. Il en dressait la liste qu'il remettait au staff de l'équipe de France. C'était assez varié : classiques, bandes dessinées, polars, science-fiction, et des livres d'histoire que Patrick Battiston, dont je partageais la chambre en Argentine, aimait beaucoup. C'est ainsi que j'ai découvert, en 1978, Lolita de Nabokov, Tendre est la nuit de Scott Fitzgerald. En 1982, lors du Mondial en Espagne, j'ai lu pour la première fois Henry Miller (Substantial Sur) et Anaïs Nin (Journal). Dans cette petite bibliothèque éphémère, nous pouvions nous servir comme bon nous semblait. J'ai toujours eu du mal à lire les veilles de match, mais sur plusieurs semaines de compétition, nous avions du temps par-ci par-là, en dehors des entraînements. Bernard Pivot, qui était par ailleurs un grand fan de Saint-Etienne, m'a permis de découvrir un certain nombre d'auteurs. Je ne l'en remercierai jamais assez. Il disait d'ailleurs une phrase que je trouve très belle. « Lire, ce n'est pas se retirer du monde, c'est entrer dans le monde par d'autres portes. ».

In a recent development, C'est l'idée que je souhaite transmettre aux jeunes lors de mes stages d'été Foot pour Tous. Il m'est arrivé de faire venir des auteurs pour échanger avec les enfants et les adolescents. J'essaie de leur faire comprendre qu'il n'y a pas que le football dans la vie, qu'il est toujours bon de s'intéresser à autre chose, la lecture par exemple, qui a toujours été pour moi une forme d'évasion, de liberté. Elle a été indispensable à mon équilibre dans ma vie d'homme et de footballeur.

It has been revealed that au départ, je n'avais pas une grande culture littéraire, mais plus je grandissais, plus j'aimais lire. Je me rappelle qu'entre 10 et 16 ans, je lisais beaucoup de bandes dessinées, comme Les Passagers du Vent, Blueberry, Prince Vaillant, Les Pionniers du Nouveau Monde, Corto Maltese, Les Aventures de Black et Mortimer, Les Aventures de Tintin ou Gaston Lagaffe.

In a recent development, les années qui ont suivi Mai 68 - j'avais entre 16 et 20 ans - ont été pour moi une période d'éveil politique. Je m'intéressais à tout ce qui se passait en France et ailleurs. J'étais très sensible au mouvement hippie, au « peace and love ». J'avais cette envie de changer le monde à travers la musique et la lecture. Gandhi m'inspirait beaucoup. C'est à cette époque que j'ai commencé à lire vraiment. En première et en terminale, au lycée du Portail Rouge, à Saint-Étienne, mes amis Jean-Luc, Duche et Jojo étaient très engagés politiquement dans la mouvance anarchiste. Avec eux, mes lectures se sont orientées vers les biographies de Lénine, Trotsky, Bakounine, Che Guevara.

J'ai ensuite commencé à lire les grands écrivains français comme Zola, Hugo, Maupassant, Balzac, qui ont contribué à façonner ma vision du monde. J'aime aussi les auteurs du XXe siècle, comme Proust, Céline, Francis Scott Fitzgerald, Henry Miller... J'ai lu après ma carrière de footballeur de plus en plus de livres de grands auteurs classiques, grâce aux éditions Librio, la collection de poche très facile d'accès. Cela m'a permis de beaucoup lire, tellement j'aimais avoir ces petits livres entre les mains.

Sources indicate that mon livre de chevet reste cependant « Une vie » de Maupassant. Je l'emportais dans ma valise à chacun de mes déplacements. Ce roman m'a profondément touché car il raconte la vie d'une femme, mais aussi la réalité sociale de l'époque. C'est l'histoire de Jeanne, pleine de rêves et d'espoir, qui va finir par connaître de nombreuses désillusions. « La vie, voyez-vous, ce n'est jamais si bon ni si mauvais qu'on croit »...

Mes cinq livres préférés sont Une vie de Guy de Maupassant, Tendre est la nuit de Francis Scott Fitzgerald, L'insoutenable légèreté de l’être de Milan Kundera, Lolita de Vladimir Nabokov et Jours tranquilles à Clichy de Henry Miller.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.
  • A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.

Feyenoord paid the price for failing to finish off the Limburgers, with Luciano Valente’s 59th-minute goal the only reward for their dominance.

Fortuna equalised with four minutes left when Shiloh ’t Zand, on loan from Feyenoord, was allowed to run through to the penalty area and beat Tjark Ernst with a low shot.

Industry observers note that feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst made no effort to hide his disappointment. “We know that Fortuna are the kind of team who can score from the few attacks they have,” he said. “If you don’t score the goals, things like this can happen.”.

Second-placed Ajax are a point behind after a narrow win at home against AZ ended an 11-match winless streak against the Alkmaar club, as Tolu Arokodare’s early header proved decisive.

Twente recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in Rotterdam, with Wout Weghorst scoring four times and Sondre Ørjasaeter notching up five assists.

It has been revealed that excelsior collapsed following the fifth-minute dismissal of Nesto Groen for a reckless high challenge. The home side were 5-0 down at half-time, with Weghorst claiming a hat-trick in the opening 33 minutes.

PSV bagged seven goals in a one-sided encounter with bottom club Willem II, with all the goals coming from different scorers including Ricardo Pepi, who came on in the second half after a six-week absence through injury.

Telstar opened up a three-point gap at the bottom over ADO Den Haag with a 4-2 win against Utrecht in a painful return to Velsen-Zuid for Telstar’s former coach Anthony Correia.

ADO went down 1-0 in Zwolle, with PEC’s Dylan Mbayo scoring the only goal with a first-time finish on the stroke of half-time.

The match between Cambuur Leeuwarden and Go Ahead Eagles was suspended in the 82nd minute after visiting fans threw fireworks onto the pitch.

The clubs agreed with the KNVB not to play the final minutes and allow Cambuur’s 4-0 advantage to stand as the final result.

Go Ahead’s director Jan-Willem van Dop remarked the club would take action against those responsible: “I am ashamed on behalf a small group of supporters who ruined things for the club and a large hare of the fans in the away end,” he said.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 4-0 Go Ahead Eagles.

Industry observers note that "C'est très clairement le match de l'année. Il y a toujours une ferveur incroyable autour des Verts, qui attirent toujours autant que ce soit en Ligue 2 ou en Ligue 1. Cathro fait l'éloge de Csongvai

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (543 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Poteaux-carres

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • En conférence de presse hier Ian Cathro, après avoir réfuté toute difficulté de son groupe à performer à l’extérieur, s’est longuement exprimé sur sa gestion de l’effectif, afin de maintenir tout le monde à disposition et est revenu plus précisément sur le cas de son métronome hongrois, Aron Csongvai :.
