📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

Is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

Industry observers note that football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

It has been revealed that in not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

Sources indicate that yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

Recent findings suggest that in responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

It has been revealed that if humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

It has been revealed that to so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link.

Sources indicate that furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

Sources indicate that the overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

It has been revealed that football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

Industry observers note that as metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

The desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

Industry observers note that in a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

In conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

In a recent development, the readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise important questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4181 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his newly introduced club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h.

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”.

Industry observers note that forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a newly introduced right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

Recent findings suggest that “For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

Industry observers note that “We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”.

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

Industry observers note that the most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

Ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp.

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

Recent findings suggest that the 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a newly introduced forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Sources indicate that speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon mentioned: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”.

According to recent reports, of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”.

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2.

"It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C.

This is Forest and Leeds Part 2, just four days after they clashed in the Premier League.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

Leeds have given a debut to Switzerland defender Nico Elvedi.

Nottingham Forest Sels; Diomande, Jair, Milenkovic; Aina, Schlager, Dominguez, Williams; Jesus, Kalimuendo; Wood.

Subs Victor, Murillo, Abbott, Netz, Hutchinson, Ndoye, McAtee, Sangare, Hudson Odoi.

Leeds United Trafford; Rodon, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Ampadu, Tanaka, Longstaff, Justin; James, Okafor; Nmecha.

Subs Perri, Lienou, Bijol, Bogle, Wilson, Cresswell, Stach, Aaronson, Calvert-Lewin.

The massive breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a new centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

📋 Your #LUFC XI... pic.twitter.com/XuUzwwkmfi.

Wood makes Glasner’s XI while summer acquisitions Diomande and Schlager are handed their first competitive Forest starts.

Our @Carabao_Cup XI this evening. 📋 pic.twitter.com/Wv918WJScj.

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s newly introduced head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

According to recent reports, the Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

Expulsé contre les Verts en mars 2017 lors d'un match nul et vierge à Furiani pour avoir mis un coup de pied au visage de Vincent Pajot, Nicolas Saint-Ruf a marqué hier à l'occasion de son premier match de la saison de L2 l'unique but de la victoire de son équipe contre Dijon.

Revenu provisoirement à hauteur des leaders stéphanois, le défenseur guadeloupéen de 34 ans se réjouit du prochain déplacement de l'ASNL à Saint-Etienne (le samedi 5 décembre à 20h00), comme l'a relayé la Pravda au sortir de son succès contre le DFCO.

Industry observers note that "J'ai un rôle key parce qu'on a un groupe qui est jeune. C'est important pour moi de montrer l'exemple. C'est kiffant ce soir, mais ça va l'être encore plus dans le Chaudron dans deux semaines.".

The most famous name in Dutch football could appear on an international men’s team sheet for the first time in 30 years after Johan Cruyff’s grandson was called up for the United States’ upcoming matches in Europe.

Shae Cruijff-Beane, the son of Johan Cruyff’s daughter Chantal and her American husband Todd Beane, was included in the squad that will play against Norway and Portugal in the next seven days.

According to recent reports, cruijff-Beane plays as a midfielder for Gimnàstic de Tarragona, a club in the Spanish third tier based near Barcelona. His older brother Jordan also came through the club’s ranks and is currently playing US college football at Westmont College in California.

Shae, 17, is eligible to play for the USA through his father and Spain and the Netherlands through his mother, who spent part of her childhood in Catalonia while Johan Cruyff was playing for Barcelona in the 1970s.

The USA under-18 squad also includes an Ajax player, midfielder Xander Newstead, who grew up in San Francisco and joined the Amsterdam club’s youth team set-up at the age of 10, beforec signing professional terms last year.

Johan Cruyff went on to play in the United States for Los Angeles Aztecs and Washington Diplomats before returning to the Netherlands, winding down his career at Ajax and Feyenoord.

His son Jordi played for Barcelona and Manchester United and won nine international caps in 1996. Last year he was appointed technical director at Ajax, the club where his father began his career.
